title: Hoffman's interface theory — perception as a desktop, not reality
summary: Podcast clip on Donald Hoffman's evolutionary game theory result: agents that perceive more than fitness payoffs lose to agents tuned only to reward, so perception works like desktop icons that hide the underlying machinery. Spacetime as interface, not ground truth.
takeaways: Fitness-tuned perception beats truth-tuned perception in Hoffman's simulations
Useful metaphor: UI icons correlate with function, not structure

title: Glenn Gould's humming — thinking music away from the piano
summary: Glenn Gould hummed audibly on nearly every recording despite Columbia engineers' mic tricks. He traced it to practising under a vacuum cleaner's noise, which taught him to hear pieces internally and learn away from the instrument; the voice is the overflow, audible on the Goldberg Variations.
takeaways: Learning music away from the instrument builds a strong inner model
Recording artifacts can become part of an artist's signature

title: Genie integer overflow — wishing for negative wishes
summary: 2D animated skit where a user exploits a genie's 2-bit wish counter: wishing for negative wishes should underflow to the maximum value, so he first upgrades the data type to 64 bits and ends with ~18 quintillion wishes. A fun explainer of integer overflow.
takeaways: An unsigned 64-bit max is about 1.8×10^19
Underflow wraps to the type's maximum value

title: Database Detective — solve crimes by writing SQL queries
summary: Database Detective is a Steam game where you solve absurd police cases by querying tables with SELECT, WHERE and JOIN to rule out suspects. Beginner-friendly with a manual, clear errors and a hint assistant, and it trains asking the right data question first. English only.
takeaways: Gamified SQL practice for aspiring analysts
The skill is choosing which table and question to start with

title: The Wrong Game — clown exercise to break perceptual autopilot
summary: Point at an object and confidently name something it isn't. A 30-second clown warm-up that jolts attention, imagination and willingness to be wrong; stumbling or going blank counts as finding the clown.
takeaways: Resist pre-planning clever answers
Use it as a quick creative warm-up before ideation

title: Bot Crossing — video-game workspace for managing 80 AI agents
summary: Open-source game UI where AI agents live on a little planet, walk around, and raise their hands when they need help; click one to see its request. Built by Jarren Rocks, with a GitHub repo, YouTube build review and botcrossing.com site.
takeaways: Spatial, game-like UIs make many agents' status glanceable
Hand-raise signals replace polling terminals

title: LLM text watermarking — how token-bias watermarks work
summary: Explains statistical watermarking: the model subtly reweights next-token probabilities with a secret key so a detector holding the key can spot the pattern over long outputs. Claims Claude Fable 5.1 watermarks everything and pitches a full-rewrite removal prompt; the claims are unverified.
takeaways: Token-bias watermarks get stronger as text gets longer
Light edits don't remove them, only full rewrites do

title: Marble extendable round dining table — 6-10 seat furniture design
summary: Product clip of a round marble dining table that extends from 100-120 cm to 150-180 cm to seat 6-10. Furniture seller promo with no narration.
takeaways: Reference for extendable round table mechanisms

title: Y-Pan — 3D-printed panoramic 35mm camera instead of a $5k XPan
summary: A maker designed the Y-Pan, a 3D-printed panoramic film camera reproducing the Hasselblad XPan's wide 35mm format. Everything except the lens is printed, parts cost about $100, it builds in about a week, and the CAD files and bill of materials are on the creator's site.
takeaways: Open CAD and a BOM make a $5k camera format buildable for ~$100
Printed mechanisms are good enough for film transport

title: Grace Hopper 1982 — the value of information as a design constraint
summary: MIT CSAIL clip of Grace Hopper predicting that data volume will grow faster than linearly and so will demand for instant access, and that the two conflict. Her answer: systems must understand the value of the information they process.
takeaways: Prioritize data by value when storage and latency conflict
Hopper called today's data tension in 1982

title: Tristan Perich's 1-Bit Symphony — music from on/off pulses on a chip
summary: 1-Bit Symphony is a composition housed in a CD case: a microchip running assembly code that outputs 1-bit on/off pulses as sound. A 695-page companion book prints the processor's cycles for the first hundredth of a second.
takeaways: Extreme constraints like a single bit of output can produce rich music
A strong reference for code-as-score work

title: Artist Grant — $1,200 unrestricted grant with no proposal
summary: Artist Grant awards $1,200 unrestricted to one visual artist three times a year since 2017. Apply by email with a website link or 3-5 images plus a short bio; $30 fee, visual arts only, open worldwide to 18+, past winners ineligible.
takeaways: The only application material is the work itself
Three deadlines a year, so there's always one coming

title: Print-on-demand art prints — sell paintings with no stock or upfront cost
summary: Upload photos to Printful, Gelato or Fine Art America, set a price, and they print, pack and ship while you keep the margin. The real work is the photo: flat, window daylight, no flash, straight on, cropped to the canvas, and list at least ten pieces.
takeaways: Shoot art flat in overcast daylight with no flash
List ten pieces so the shop looks like a shop
You usually keep print rights to sold originals

title: OSINT tools — photo geolocation, exposed AI servers, leak search
summary: Three unnamed open-source OSINT tools: one geolocates photos without metadata, one scans the internet for unauthenticated AI servers and scores their exposure on a globe, and one searches leaked logins, wallets and dark web mentions by name or company. Links are comment-gated.
takeaways: Unauthenticated AI servers are a growing exposure class
Tool names aren't given, so you need to find equivalents

title: Nagarjuna and Rovelli — emptiness meets relational quantum mechanics
summary: Carlo Rovelli devotes a chapter of Helgoland to Nagarjuna's Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way: nothing has independent existence, only relations. That mirrors Rovelli's relational interpretation where objects have properties only relative to other objects.
takeaways: Relational QM drops observer-independent properties
Read Helgoland for the physics-philosophy bridge

title: Autonomous AI pentest agent — plain-English prompt to verified exploit
summary: An unnamed ~600-star GitHub repo where you describe a target in one sentence and an agent finds a vulnerability, runs the exploit and writes the report, across 13 AI providers. Every claimed finding is verified against real tool output. Authorized targets only.
takeaways: Verifying findings against real tool output curbs hallucinated vulns
Only run against systems you're authorized to test

title: Sharp Memory Display — per-pixel memory LCD for low-power hardware
summary: Sharp memory displays store each pixel's state, so they only need a tiny maintenance signal. That makes them near e-paper in power, reflective for sunlight readability, yet fast enough for ~50fps, as on the Playdate.
takeaways: Pick it for battery projects with mostly static screens
Faster than e-paper and readable outdoors

title: Orbiter — open-source smartphone 3D scanner for print-ready parts
summary: Orbiter is an open-source rig and workflow from Raw Mechatronics for accurate 3D digitization with a smartphone camera. Scan an object, design around it and print a part that fits the first time.
takeaways: Accurate scanning closes the loop for custom-fit prints
Build-it-yourself open project, still evolving

title: DIY founder PR — agent-scraped journalist requests and tailored pitches
summary: Have an agent scrape journalist request sites into a database, pull each journalist's last ten articles, draft a similar story angle featuring you, and send short emails. Lessons: short non-AI-sounding pitches win, offer visibility, do ideation yourself, claim your Google profile, and it's a volume game.
takeaways: Short emails get more replies than long pitches
Give the model example emails so it doesn't sound like AI
Pitch angles close to what the journalist already writes

title: Peppa Cam — DIY Raspberry Pi handheld LiDAR scanner
summary: A homemade handheld LiDAR scanner from a Raspberry Pi, a LiDAR sensor and a 3D-printed housing, mapping buildings, caves, gardens and trees without proprietary software. Build plan with wiring, code and CAD is comment-gated.
takeaways: Handheld LiDAR is buildable for far less than a Leica
Open formats avoid proprietary lock-in

title: Hand-cut kitchen tile mosaic — materials and process from a first build
summary: First hand-cut mosaic: 2x2 cm Winckelmans tiles cut with two nippers, glued to fiberglass mesh with Titebond, mounted on Knauf Aquapanel with Mapei Adesilex P10, cured 30 hours, brown grout, and a 5mm silicone expansion gap. Took a month, not two weeks.
takeaways: Assemble on fiberglass mesh, then mount
Leave a perimeter expansion gap sealed with silicone
Budget twice the time you expect
